sections.h2: What comes first when a Horsham homeowner decides to sell?
sections.html:
Horsham Township asks every seller of a residential property to complete a township inspection and certification before settlement, so build that step into your timeline from day one. The rest of the sale follows the usual Pennsylvania pattern, with Montgomery County handling assessment, recording and transfer tax.

Horsham is about ten miles north of Center City Philadelphia, with an estimated 27,882 residents. Roughly 71.5 percent of homes are owner-occupied, a typical owned home is valued at $473,100, and typical rent is $1,573. At those values, a delay of even a few weeks costs real money in carrying costs and interest.

A fast sale to a cash buyer, a listing and a for-sale-by-owner deal all need the township certification below, because the rule attaches to the property transfer and not to the type of buyer.

The township requires an inspection of every residential property before a transfer. The application and fee go to the Horsham Township Municipal Building at 1025 Horsham Road within the 90 days before settlement.

  • A township inspector checks the curb and sidewalk in front of the property.
  • The street address must be posted and easy to see from the road.
  • The seller certifies that working smoke detectors are in the house.

Schedule the inspection early enough to fix a cracked sidewalk slab or a missing house number before settlement. Questions go to the Code Enforcement department at (215) 643-3131.

The township also issues tax certifications through its tax collector. Send your contact details, the parcel number, the property address, the owner's name and a $30 check per parcel made out to Horsham Township, plus a stamped return envelope if you want it mailed. A title company normally handles this, but a seller handling the sale directly will need to order it.

sections.h2: Commute and neighborhood notes for your listing
sections.html:
Buyers here shop by commute and by corporate campus, so say so in your listing. Easton Road (Route 611) runs north to south through the eastern side, Horsham Road (Route 463) crosses the center, and Welsh Road (Route 63), Limekiln Pike (Route 152) and Bethlehem Pike (Route 309) frame the edges. The Willow Grove interchange of the Pennsylvania Turnpike sits just south in Upper Moreland Township.

SEPTA bus Route 55 follows Route 611, and a weekday rush hour shuttle called h.o.p.s. connects the office parks to the Fort Washington station on the Lansdale/Doylestown Regional Rail line. The township's villages include Horsham, Hallowell, Prospectville and Maple Glen, and the Hatboro-Horsham School District serves the area.

sections.h2: Montgomery County assessments and tax sales
sections.html:
The county Board of Assessment Appeals sets the values behind county, township and school bills. Yearly appeals are due August 1 and change the tax year after. That same August 1 date applies to real estate tax exemption applications. State law requires annual appeals to be decided by October 31 so changes reach the rolls and taxing bodies by November 15.

The board advises mailing deadline filings with a hand-cancelled postmark, a Certificate of Mailing or certified mail, because postal delays can mark a timely envelope late. You can also hand deliver in Norristown on weekdays between 8:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. The board's phone line is 610-278-3761.

If the house carries unpaid taxes, the county Tax Claim Bureau enters the picture.

Montgomery County Tax Claim Bureau sales
Sale typeWhen heldWhat a buyer gets
Upset saleEach September and DecemberThe property subject to its liens
Judicial saleAt least once a year, in August and DecemberThe property free and clear

Clear any delinquency before listing so it does not surface at closing.

Unpaid taxes do not block a sale, but the balance has to be cleared at or before closing. Ask the title company for a payoff figure early, and settle it from your sale proceeds if you cannot pay it beforehand. Once a delinquency reaches the Tax Claim Bureau, the house can end up in an upset or judicial sale, and you lose control of the timing and the price.

If you are behind and short on time, a cash sale with a closing date you pick can get the balance paid before the next sale date. Keep the Bureau's September and December upset sale dates in mind when you plan, and call the county before then to confirm your exact balance.

Also check for unpaid township items. A title company will flag them, but finding them yourself first means no surprises on the settlement statement.

Here is the order most Horsham sellers follow. Start by calling Code Enforcement and asking for the transfer inspection application. Book the inspection and fix whatever it turns up, which is usually a curb, a sidewalk slab or a house number. Order the tax certification if you are not using a title company. Review your assessment, and if you think it is too high, remember that the appeal deadline is August 1 and only changes the following tax year.

Once you have an accepted offer, the buyer's title company orders the search and prepares the settlement statement. Read the statement line by line. Sellers here handle large transfer tax bills at these values, so confirm who pays each share before you sign. After settlement, the deed is recorded in Montgomery County.

Because the township certification must be submitted within the 90 days before settlement, avoid filing it too early. An application filed months in advance may have to be redone if closing slips.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale the better choice in Horsham?
sections.html:
A cash sale helps most when the property does not fit a conventional buyer's loan, or when the seller cannot wait through showings. Examples are a house with deferred roof or mechanical work, an estate property that needs to close before the next tax bill, or a seller relocating out of the area.

Because Horsham values are high, compare any cash figure with a full net sheet: list price, agent commission, transfer tax, repairs to pass the township inspection, and carrying cost. If you would like a cash figure for your Horsham house, Cash Home Buyers CA can provide one to set against that sheet.

A cash buyer skips the showings and the loan approval, so the closing date can follow your schedule. The township certification still applies, since the rule follows the property. Ask the buyer to confirm who will schedule the inspection and who pays for any sidewalk or address fix, and get that agreement in writing before you commit to a closing date.

faqs.q: Is an inspection required to sell a house in Horsham Township?
faqs.a: Yes. The Residential Property Transfer Certification Program requires an inspection of every residential property before transfer, covering the curb, the sidewalk and the posted address, plus a seller certification of working smoke detectors. Submit it within 90 days before settlement.

faqs.q: How much does a Horsham tax certification cost?
faqs.a: The township's tax collector charges $30 per parcel, paid by check to Horsham Township. Include the parcel number, property address and owner name, and say how you want the certification returned.

faqs.q: What date closes the yearly Montgomery County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: August 1, and the result applies to the next tax year.
The Hatboro-Horsham School District serves the township, along with neighboring Hatboro. Its schools include Keith Valley Middle School and Hatboro-Horsham Senior High School.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Horsham house with unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, but the unpaid amount must be cleared at or before closing. Taxes that reach the county Tax Claim Bureau can put the property into an upset or judicial sale, so settle the balance before then.
